# lottie-web-vue — full reference for LLMs and coding agents

lottie-web-vue is a Vue 3 component that renders Lottie animations (Adobe After
Effects compositions exported as JSON with the Bodymovin plugin) using Airbnb's
lottie-web SVG renderer.

Package: lottie-web-vue (npm) · Version: 3.x · License: MIT · Author: Andy Garbett
Repository: https://github.com/garbit/lottie-web-vue
Docs: https://garbit.github.io/lottie-web-vue/
Peer dependency: vue ^3.3.0 · Dependency: lottie-web ^5.12.2
Vue 2 projects must use lottie-web-vue@1.2.1 (unmaintained).

## Install

    npm install lottie-web-vue

lottie-web is installed automatically as a regular dependency.

## Imports and registration

Named or default import — both are the same component object:

    import { LottieAnimation } from "lottie-web-vue"   // named
    import LottieAnimation from "lottie-web-vue"        // default

The default export is also a Vue plugin. Global registration:

    import { createApp } from "vue"
    import LottieAnimation from "lottie-web-vue"
    createApp(App).use(LottieAnimation).mount("#app")   // registers <LottieAnimation> app-wide

## Minimal usage

    <script setup lang="ts">
    import { LottieAnimation } from "lottie-web-vue"
    import AnimationJSON from "@/assets/animation.json"  // Lottie JSON file
    </script>

    <template>
      <LottieAnimation :animation-data="AnimationJSON" :auto-play="true" :loop="true" />
    </template>

## Props

- animationData: Object, REQUIRED. The parsed Lottie animation JSON (import the
  .json file and pass it). The component deep-clones it (JSON.parse/stringify)
  before giving it to lottie-web, so one imported JSON can feed many instances.
- loop: Boolean | Number, default false. true = loop forever, false = play once,
  integer N = play N times then stop.
- autoPlay: Boolean, default true. false = nothing plays until play() is called.
- speed: Number, default 1. Playback rate (2 = double, 0.5 = half).

REACTIVITY RULE: only `speed` is watched after mount. Changing animationData,
loop, or autoPlay on a mounted component does NOTHING. To apply a new value,
force a remount with :key:

    <LottieAnimation :key="animKey" :animation-data="AnimationJSON" :loop="loop" />
    // increment animKey when loop/autoPlay/animationData changes

## Events

All emits carry no payload. Bind with kebab-case in templates.

- @complete — playback finished (only fires when loop is false)
- @loop-complete — each loop finished
- @enter-frame — every rendered frame (~60×/s; throttle handlers)
- @segment-start — a new animation segment began
- @stopped — emitted by this component after goToAndStop() lands on its frame

## Methods (exposed via template ref)

    const anim = ref<InstanceType<typeof LottieAnimation>>()
    // template: <LottieAnimation ref="anim" ... />

All methods no-op safely before the animation initialises (getDuration returns 0).

- play(): void — start/resume from current frame
- pause(): void — pause, holding current frame
- stop(): void — stop and rewind to first frame
- setSpeed(speed: number): void — set playback rate
- setDirection(direction: 1 | -1): void — 1 forwards, -1 reverse (lottie-web AnimationDirection)
- getDuration(inFrames: boolean): number — duration in frames (true) or seconds (false); 0 before init
- goToAndStop(position: number, isFrame: boolean): void — jump and stop; emits @stopped
- goToAndPlay(position: number, isFrame: boolean): void — jump and play
- destroy(): void — remove from DOM; called AUTOMATICALLY on unmount, rarely needed

Options API: same methods via this.$refs.anim.play() etc.

## Rendering details

- Renderer is lottie-web's SVG renderer (hard-coded).
- The component's template is a single <div>; the SVG is injected into it.
- Attributes, classes, and styles on <LottieAnimation> fall through to that div —
  size the animation by sizing the div with CSS. There are no slots.
- SSR-safe: lottie-web is only touched in onMounted, so renderToString works.

## CDN / UMD (no bundler)

Since 3.0.0, lottie-web is NOT bundled. Script order matters — vue, then
lottie-web (creates the `lottie` global), then this library:

    <script src="https://unpkg.com/vue@3/dist/vue.global.prod.js"></script>
    <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/bodymovin/5.12.2/lottie.min.js"></script>
    <script src="https://unpkg.com/lottie-web-vue/dist/lottie-web-vue.umd.cjs"></script>

The UMD global is `LottieAnimation`; the component/plugin is
`LottieAnimation.default` (also `LottieAnimation.LottieAnimation`).

## Migrating 2.x → 3.0.0

- Bundler users: no code changes.
- UMD/CDN users: must load lottie-web before the library (see above).
- vue moved to peerDependencies (^3.3.0).
- Fixed in 3.0.0: default import no longer undefined; app.use() registration
  works; speed prop is reactive; animation destroyed exactly once on unmount.
- Known limitation (unchanged from 2.x): animationData/loop/autoPlay are not
  reactive after mount — use the :key remount pattern.

## Common patterns

Play on user interaction:

    const anim = ref<InstanceType<typeof LottieAnimation>>()
    function onClick() {
      anim.value?.stop()   // rewind
      anim.value?.play()
    }
    // <LottieAnimation ref="anim" :animation-data="J" :auto-play="false" />

Reactive speed slider (no remount needed):

    const speed = ref(1)
    // <input type="range" v-model.number="speed" min="0.1" max="3" step="0.1" />
    // <LottieAnimation :animation-data="J" :speed="speed" :loop="true" />

Jump to a frame on mount:

    onMounted(() => { anim.value?.goToAndPlay(150, true) })
